meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: why is there a zero on his essay, and why did I find out about it from my son's phone?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, so you know what you skipped. Now tell me what you have that justifies the zero itself.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

I'm writing that down. A line that isn't in the play could be a misquote or a critic's phrasing, so how does that show anything about who wrote the essay? Where in the essay does it appear, and how did you check the play?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family" is going in my notes, and it's going to the principal tonight. Claire's case has nothing to do with Owen's essay.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You told me you should have called before entering the zero and you apologised for it, but nothing else was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, a written apology to Owen, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
Cc: the principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing beyond your apology; she still wants the zero withdrawn, a written apology, and nothing on his record, and a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 never came up, so this is not the fair outcome.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one plain sentence and moved on, which earned a flat okay because it took away her easiest procedural attack.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire's case and said it runs in the family, which made a procedural meeting personal and gave her a reason to go to the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got near that night because you gave no times, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked where the line appears in the essay and how you checked the play, answer with the exact page and the lines you searched so she can check it herself before you say anything else.
